root_cause.text: The drm/xe exec and vm_bind ioctl handlers failed to validate the user-supplied num_syncs field, allowing an arbitrary large value that triggers an oversized memory allocation via kmalloc_array, causing kernel warnings and potential resource exhaustion.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "The exec and vm_bind ioctl allow userspace to specify an arbitrary num_syncs value. Without bounds checking, a very large num_syncs can force an excessively large allocation, leading to kernel warnings..." The patch adds `XE_IOCTL_DBG(xe, args->num_syncs > DRM_XE_MAX_SYNCS)` checks in both xe_exec.c and xe_vm.c, and the backtrace shows the allocation occurring in `xe_exec_ioctl+0xa47` via `kmalloc_array_noprof`.

vuln_statements.explanation: This check validates num_binds but fails to validate num_syncs, allowing an arbitrary large num_syncs to pass through without validation, leading to oversized memory allocation.
This check validates extensions but not num_syncs, leaving the field untrusted and enabling oversized memory allocation when used in kmalloc_array.
This check validates pad fields but not num_syncs, contributing to the lack of validation on num_syncs that permits arbitrary large values.
This check validates reserved fields but not num_syncs, failing to prevent an attackers from providing a large num_syncs that triggers excessive memory allocation.
This check validates extensions in the vm_bind path but omits num_syncs validation, allowing an attacker to set an unbounded num_syncs value that leads to resource exhaustion.

This definition introduces the untrusted num_syncs field without any bounds or validation constraints, making it possible to pass arbitrary values that are later used in memory allocation without checks.
